comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C1, C2, C4 regarding PKM2 nuclear translocation in EAE. Both evaluations find the evidence convincing and well-supported by immunofluorescence and quantitative data. Reviewers specifically praise the experimental design and controls.

Perfect agreement on claims C5-C12, C97 regarding DASA-58 effects on astrocyte activation. Both evaluations recognize the comprehensive battery of experiments (immunofluorescence, glucose/lactate, western blot, CCK-8, EdU, qPCR) as strongly supporting the claims about reduced proliferation, glycolysis, and inflammatory cytokine secretion.

Strong agreement on claims C14-C19 regarding pathway activation (STAT3, NF-κB, c-myc phosphorylation and nuclear retention). OpenEval focuses on C14-C19 while peer review includes C13 (background). Both find the mechanistic evidence convincing with appropriate complementary techniques (immunofluorescence, western blot, fractionation, co-IP).

Agreement on claims C21-C23 regarding mass spectrometry identification of TRIM21. OpenEval also includes C24 (bioinformatic analyses). Peer reviewers support the proteomic findings as part of the comprehensive experimental approach, noting how multiple techniques complement each other.

Strong agreement on claims C25-C30 regarding TRIM21-PKM2 direct interaction. Both evaluations recognize the use of multiple complementary techniques (docking, endogenous IP, reciprocal co-IP, domain mapping) as providing convincing evidence for this novel regulatory mechanism.

Perfect agreement on claims C32-C36, C63, C99 regarding TRIM21 upregulation in EAE astrocytes. Both evaluations praise the multi-modal validation approach using scRNA-seq, public datasets, western blot, and immunofluorescence as a key strength of the study.

Agreement on claims C37-C40, C73 regarding TRIM21-mediated K63-ubiquitination and PKM2 nuclear translocation. OpenEval focuses on mechanistic evidence from fractionation and IP experiments. Peer review (R6) includes additional claims C64, C91, C98 and emphasizes this as a novel regulatory mechanism adding to current knowledge about ubiquitination-induced PKM2 relocalization.

Strong agreement on claims C41-C48, C100 regarding TRIM21 effects on PKM2-dependent glycolysis and proliferation. OpenEval also includes C98. Both evaluations recognize the comprehensive functional assays and particularly note the importance of DASA-58 rescue experiments in establishing the mechanistic link.

Perfect agreement on claims C49-C57, C87, C88, C101 regarding in vivo TRIM21 knockdown therapeutic effects in EAE. Both evaluations support the findings on disease severity, CNS inflammation, demyelination, and astrocyte/microglia responses. Both recognize the comprehensive in vivo validation as a strength.

Agreement on claims C58-C60, C79, C102 regarding TEPP-46 therapeutic efficacy. Both evaluations support the findings but peer reviewers note this confirms previous findings in T cells (incremental novelty). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED while peer review is also SUPPORTED, recognizing this as independent pharmacological validation of the mechanism.

Both evaluations address therapeutic translation claims C80, C89, C92, C126 with UNCERTAIN status. OpenEval includes C85 while peer review includes C62, C90. Both note that while EAE data support efficacy, translation to human MS requires additional validation. Peer reviewers specifically raise concerns about PKM2-independent TRIM21 effects and note in vivo experiments address TRIM21 and PKM2 independently.

Partial overlap on claims C62, C90 regarding novelty and mechanistic conclusions. OpenEval rates these as SUPPORTED synthesis of findings (also includes C91), while peer review groups them with therapeutic translation claims (C80, C89, C92, C126) and rates as UNCERTAIN, expressing reservations about complete mechanistic resolution.
OpenEval evaluates claims C3, C93, C94 as SUPPORTED methodological background with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific methodological claims.

OpenEval evaluates 44 claims (C13, C20, C31, C65-C72, C74-C78, C82-C84, C95-C96, C103-C125) as SUPPORTED background knowledge and literature review. While peer review mentions C13 in R3, there is no comprehensive peer evaluation of this extensive set of background claims.
OpenEval evaluates claim C81 regarding microglial metabolism as SUPPORTED established knowledge providing context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific background claim.
OpenEval evaluates claim C86 regarding PKM2-p65 interaction as SUPPORTED by immunoprecipitation data (Figure 3E). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific interaction claim.

Minimal overlap on claim C24 only. OpenEval R4 addresses C21-C24 (mass spec and bioinformatics), while peer R4 addresses C24-C30 (TRIM21-PKM2 interaction identification and validation). Both support their respective claim sets, but they largely address different aspects of the TRIM21 discovery.
